asks: What does Silo do so that the Mac does not sleep while computers run?
answer: While a computer runs and the Mac is on power, Silo holds the Mac awake, as `caffeinate` does. It cannot stop a closed MacBook from sleeping unless an external display is attached, so it says so when you start a computer on such a Mac. Every sleep and wake of the Mac is written in the record, so a night with no work shows why.
